title: Compact laptop price and pooled-text residual model
question: Can pooled article features add useful error reduction to an independently fitted compact price forecast within laptop resource targets?
configuration: compact_features.py exports a checksum/signature-verified existing pooled cache without LLM loading; train_compact.py fits price first, freezes it, then fits the tiny text correction. 82598 total parameters for 2048-dimensional text; training-only feature normalization; H35/70/140 endpoints; three past-date donor controls and paired date-block intervals. Portable NPZ with --include-prices plus receipt allows local training without raw articles/backbones; default run_local.ps1 mode is multimodal.
finding: Feature integrity/mapping, donor chronology, frozen-price residual fitting and aligned text-control tests passed on synthetic fixtures. Full real-data training/evaluation pending.
limitations: Actual RTX4060 CUDA synthetic execution passed, but no real-market accuracy, T4 execution or raw-article encoding latency is verified. Current shared CUDA packages are reused through a working project-local interpreter; no shared environment was overwritten. Timestamp availability remains unverified.

evidence.label: Synthetic RTX4060 execution timing, not quality
